faqs.question: What is this system used for?
faqs.answer: It's a complete transient absorption spectrometer for laser flash photolysis, measuring short-lived excited states and reaction intermediates from nanoseconds to seconds.

faqs.question: Does this system include a laser?
faqs.answer: No, the laser is sourced separately. Everything else needed to run laser flash photolysis, the light source, monochromator, digitizer, detector, and software, is included.

faqs.question: Why does the system use a continuous lamp instead of pulsing it?
faqs.answer: Continuous illumination improves signal-to-noise, extends lamp life, gives cleaner signal baselines, improves detector linearity, and reduces sample degradation compared to pulsed-lamp operation.

faqs.question: How do I choose between the three wavelength range options?
faqs.answer: Match your chromophore's absorption range: UV (240-730nm) for standard UV-visible work, RED (310-800nm) for red-shifted species, or OF (330-800nm) for the broadest single-range coverage.

faqs.question: How do I set up connection-free laser synchronization?
faqs.answer: The system uses a fiber optic sensor for laser-sensing pre-trigger detection, so no hard-wired trigger cable is needed between the laser and the spectrometer.

faqs.question: What timescales can this system actually measure?
faqs.answer: From under 10 nanoseconds using the built-in amplifier out to millisecond-scale processes.

faqs.question: Can I run diffuse reflectance measurements?
faqs.answer: Yes, if purchased as an additional option alongside absorption mode, allowing switching between the two once both are installed.

faqs.question: How long does it take to receive this system?
faqs.answer: Lead time runs 8 to 14 weeks from order.

faqs.question: What is the price of this system in India?
faqs.answer: Get in touch and Inkarp will put together a quote around your wavelength range, temperature control, and measurement mode.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of this system in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the Luzchem Laser Flash Photolysis system in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

sections.title: Continuous Lamp Design and Measurement Modes
sections.description: Pulsing a probe lamp to match a laser sounds like the obvious approach, and it's exactly what most systems do. This one doesn't, and that difference shows up in the data.

cards.title: A lamp that lasts through your study
cards.description: No pulsing stress on the source

paragraphs: A continuously running xenon lamp gives a stable, always-on probe beam rather than one that has to fire in sync with a laser pulse. That stability is what improves signal-to-noise and gives cleaner baselines, and because the lamp isn't being repeatedly stressed by pulsing, it lasts longer and behaves more linearly as a detector reference. The sample benefits too, seeing less cumulative light exposure than it would under a pulsed lamp regime, which means less photodegradation over the course of a study.

heroParagraphs: Most flash photolysis systems pulse the probe lamp in sync with the laser to get enough brightness during the measurement window, and that pulsing takes a toll. This system runs the lamp continuously instead.

That single design choice pays off five ways at once: better signal-to-noise, a longer-lived lamp, cleaner signal baselines, more linear detector behavior, and less photodegradation of the sample from repeated flashing. Measurements span from nanoseconds out to full seconds, synchronization with laser pulses happens connection-free, and the whole system fits a genuinely compact footprint despite being complete and turnkey. The laser itself is sourced separately.

Wavelength range is set at order, UV, red-extended, or the broadest OF range, with temperature control available for sensitive kinetics, and absorption and diffuse reflectance modes switchable once both are on the system.
